stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan: Three trains rescheduled, schools shut across six Odisha districts
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Three trains rescheduled, schools shut across six Odisha districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan is approaching the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast with winds of up to 110 kmph, prompting train rescheduling and school closures across six Odisha districts.

With winds reaching speeds of up to 100 kmph and gusts likely to touch 110 kmph, Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is bearing down on the eastern coastline, prompting authorities in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up precautionary measures.
The approaching storm has already disrupted railway schedules, while educational institutions across six Odisha districts will remain closed for three days as the state prepares for its impact.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Akvan, currently positioned over the westcentral Bay of Bengal, is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Thursday, November 19.
The system is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, with gusts reaching 110 kmph.
The approaching cyclone has prompted railway authorities to revise the departure timings of three trains scheduled to operate on Thursday.
- Train No. 18046 Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express, originally scheduled to leave at 8.40 am on November 19, will now depart at 3.40 pm on the same day.
- Similarly, Train No. 12704 Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express, which was scheduled to depart at 3.55 pm, has been rescheduled to 5.55 pm.
- Train No. 15227 SMVT Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express will also operate behind schedule.
The train, originally scheduled to leave at 12.30 am on Thursday, will now depart at 8.30 am.

As part of its precautionary response, the Odisha government has ordered the closure of all government, government-aided and private schools, along with Anganwadi centres, in six districts from November 19 to November 21.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the state administration was fully prepared to tackle the approaching weather system and had initiated the necessary response measures.

stories.headline: Flood-hit Florida braces for more rain as roads go underwater, schools shut
stories.title: Flood-hit Florida braces for more rain as roads go underwater, schools shut
stories.summary: Southeast Florida is grappling with severe flooding and relentless rainfall, significantly affecting the lives of residents. Emergency services are engaged in high-water rescues as rivers approach critical capacity, leading to perilous situations. Schools in Broward and Miami-Dade counties have suspended classes, and transportation is heavily impacted. A flood watch remains active, with forecasts predicting additional rainfall in the coming days.

stories.headline: Govt performing in best capacity with no excuses, BJP attempting to weaken Govt: CM
stories.title: Govt performing in best capacity with no excuses, BJP attempting to weaken Govt: CM
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday said that government was performing in best capacity with no member of government giving a coward excuse of being a UT government and promises made in the election manifesto were being fulfilled. In his statement during rally, CM Omar said that Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) was leaving no stone upturned in demeaning the J&K government and humiliating it but ground reality was that their government was working in the best manner and was also fulfilling its promises. "We have given six free cylinders, have given relief in the form of 200 free electricity units through solar, hiked social welfare pensions as well as monetary aid for marriage assistance scheme, provided free travel for women in government buses," he said stressing that all the promises made in the election manifesto would be fulfilled. "The main thing is that we are part of UT with limited resources but none of my colleage ever gave an excuse of it as we are not cowards," the CM said. Accusing BJP of attempting to humilate the J&K government, he questioned difference in protocol positions of elected representatives in Warrant of Precedence of a state and UT. "If a Chief Secretary and a High Court Chief Justice enjoys same position in Warrant of Precedence of a state as well as a UT, then why is there sharp difference between positions of elected representatives," CM Omar said. He also talked about resumption of Darbar Move practice in Jammu and Kashmir to benefit economy of Jammu province as well as shifting examination pattern of Kashmir winter areas to October-November session. "We even followed the project of Mughal Road tunnel in best possible manner and our colleagues including Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary remained in contact with Delhi and it is a result of our efforts that the DPR making is in process and will be approved soon and you will see work on it after which round the year traffic movement will be possible," the CM said. Addressing the public rally in Mendhar, he accused the Centre of not taking any solid step regarding reservation matter of J&K despite submission of cabinet committee reports multiple times. "The report of our cabinet committee on reservation was submitted at appropriate quarters. However, as we are a UT, the report was returned to us with some objections which we covered. This has happened multiple times. We are submitting reports and they return with objections. We reply to objections and then a new query is put. This all is being done only to stall a solution," CM Omar said.

stories.headline: Mughal road tunnel work to commence soon: CM
stories.title: Mughal road tunnel work to commence soon: CM
stories.summary: Mendhar (Poonch), Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday stated that the work on the Mughal road tunnel would commence very soon and in the coming years, the road would remain open throughout the year, ensuring all-weather connectivity between the two regions. He said that providing all-weather connectivity between the Pir Panjal region and Kashmir through the historic Mughal road was the dream of former Chief Minister Sher-e-Kashmir Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. He was addressing the gathering after dedicating 13 development projects worth Rs 92.84 Cr to the people of Mendhar in the frontier district of Poonch, giving fresh impetus to infrastructure development and strengthening essential public services in the border constituency. The projects, spread across road connectivity, power infrastructure, flood protection, education and drinking water supply, include eight inaugurations and five foundation stone-laying ceremonies, reflecting the government’s continued focus on improving basic amenities and extending development to remote and border areas. Addressing a large public gathering, the Chief Minister highlighted the key initiatives undertaken by the government to fulfil its commitments to the people, particularly in social welfare, public transport, education, recruitment and restoration of the Darbar Move. He reiterated that the restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir remained a key commitment, saying he had consistently reminded the Prime Minister and Union Home Minister of the assurance made to the people, both during their visits to Jammu and Kashmir and in meetings in Delhi. Highlighting the implementation of welfare commitments, Omar Abdullah said the government had initiated the provision of six free LPG cylinders annually to the poorest households, as part of its promise of 12 cylinders. He also referred to the progress made towards providing 200 units of free electricity through solar energy. Emphasising measures aimed at easing the financial burden on women, he said free travel in government buses had been introduced for women, particularly benefiting students commuting to schools and colleges. The government had also enhanced social security benefits, including old-age and widow pensions, besides increasing marriage assistance for economically weaker families. On employment and reservation, the Chief Minister said the government had taken up recruitment-related commitments and constituted a Cabinet Sub-Committee to examine reservation-related issues and address concerns in this regard. Among the major projects, the Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for a 50 MVA, 132/33 KV Grid Sub-Station at Mendhar, being executed by JKP
